targetAudience.primary: Open-source maintainers designing skill, plugin and approval systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands extensions, filesystem paths and approval gates.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Repository-controlled text or path-like data can impersonate user authority unless invocation and provenance are qualified by the host.

whyNow: A merged OpenAI Codex Guardian v2 change records invoked user-owned skills as bounded approval evidence only after canonical trusted-root checks, with explicit negative coverage for repository forgeries and symlink escapes.

externalHook.description: A path under a trusted root can establish bounded origin while still saying nothing about the exact bytes, meaning or freshness of approval.

coreProposition: An invoked skill should influence authorization only after the host records the actual invocation and verifies resource provenance against an authority-owned trusted root; canonical location proves a bounded origin under that trust model, not content identity, semantic safety, immutability or contemporaneous user approval.

originalValue.description: Separates occurrence, location provenance, content identity, semantic safety and current approval so one verified dimension cannot silently stand in for the others.

readerTakeaway: Record the host-observed invocation, canonical resource and trust-root decision; add a content digest when replay matters; keep repository assertions non-authorizing and expose evidence truncation.

supported: Guardian records a skill only after host resolution through configured trusted user roots.
Canonicalization and root containment reject repository skills and symlink escapes on the demonstrated path.
Guardian receives a bounded deduplicated path list rather than privileged full skill bodies.
Maintainer tests cover trusted invocation and negative provenance cases.
unsupported: Semantic safety of trusted skill contents
Immutable identity of the invoked bytes
A universal filesystem or authorization standard
uncertain: Revocation behavior after a trusted skill changes
How later audit proves the exact version invoked
How omitted evidence is surfaced when budgets truncate the list

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article presents a general open-source extension-provenance pattern without first-party project dependency.

decisionReason: The merged implementation and tests support a concrete provenance qualification mechanism and expose a useful multi-dimensional evidence boundary.
